messages:
mia: quick sanity check — customer sees auth failures only on Edge (Vercel Edge Functions). Node + Serverless OK. Error at runtime: "TypeError: Headers is not a constructor". Bundling with Vite, TS SDK ESM entry. Anyone seen fetch/Headers polyfill collisions? cc @sam @jordan

sam: can you paste the minimal repro + package.json/build config? `Headers is not a constructor` usually means something overwrote the native Headers (node-fetch polyfills do that) or a mismatched runtime shim.

mia: repro notes: Next 14 edge API route, TS sdk imported like `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`. package.json has "type":"module". Using vite build with esbuild target. No explicit node-fetch. Runtime stack: auth.ts:42 -> auth handshake -> new Headers(init.headers) throws.

jordan: edge runtimes expose WHATWG fetch. If a node polyfill ran at bundle time it can serialize/replace Headers with a stub object. Grep for `polyfill` or `node-fetch` imports in deps.

lee: ^ exactly. I once hit this: a transitive dep pulled `node-fetch/polyfill` via a plugin. The polyfill assigns `global.Headers = HeadersShim` which breaks native. Solution: remove polyfill for edge builds or guard with `if (!globalThis.process)` etc.

mia: i grepped — found `node-polyfills` plugin in infra config, it injects `import 'node-fetch/polyfill'` for legacy builds. removing that from edge pipeline fixes the repro locally.

sam: good find. For SDK-level mitigation, we should: 1) avoid importing node-specific shims in any ESM entry intended for edge; 2) add a runtime check that bails with a clear error if Headers/fetch shape is unexpected (and logs guidance: "remove node-fetch polyfills for edge"); 3) document bundler flags for Next/Vite.

jordan: small code snippet for a defensive check we used:
```js
if (typeof fetch !== 'function' || typeof Headers === 'undefined' || typeof Headers.prototype.append !== 'function') {
  throw new Error('Redwood SDK: detected incompatible fetch/Headers. Do not include node-fetch polyfills when targeting edge runtimes.');
}
```

mia: will add that to auth init. Also will add a docs blurb: "Edge builds — do not include node-fetch or global fetch polyfills; set your bundler/browser field appropriately." link to Vercel best practices would help.

anya: Vercel doc: https://vercel.com/docs/concepts/functions/edge-runtimes — they explicitly warn against node polyfills. :+1:

lee: FYI another bundler quirk: forcing CJS -> ESM transform can introduce `require` wrappers that pull in `globalThis` shims. Recommend using the SDK's esm entrypoint in consumers (package.json `exports` should map `"import"` to ESM, `"require"` to CJS).

sam: action items: mia open PR to docs + add runtime guard; i will open a tiny SDK PR that logs a clear error and updates exports to ensure ESM edge entrypoint has zero node-only deps. jordan/lee can review. ci-bot will run QA.

ci-bot: QA pipeline triggered for branch mia/edge-polyfill-fix — status: queued

mia: thanks all — i'll ping when PR is up. If this hits customers, quick workaround: remove node polyfill plugin from edge bundle and redeploy. :raised_hands:
